items.title: LineageOS 24 PC port brings Android 17 to your spare laptop
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Developer Mateus Seiboth has put together a port of LineageOS 24 for x86 PCs. 
 The release can run of a USB stick, and supports systems with as little as 4GB of RAM. 
 GPU support is a little more hit-and-miss, with AMD cards currently favored. 

Android fans have a new device category to put on their holiday shopping lists this year, with Googlebook deals already arriving for Black Friday , but if you can’t afford to pick up some new hardware right now, we just found what might be the next best thing, courtesy of a project to bring LineageOS 24 to your existing PC.

It’s only been a little over a month now since we saw LineageOS get its big Android 17 update , and today we spotted a project that developer Mateus Seiboth is sharing over on Reddit: a version of LineageOS 24 for your x86 computer.
items.t: LineageOS 24 PC port brings Android 17 to your spare laptop

YouTube is not done tinkering with its mobile app, and the streaming giant’s latest redesign is making the platform’s Home feed a lot more chaotic.

It’s been less than a month since YouTube began moving the Subscription tab away from the bottom navigation bar, and users, very clearly, weren’t happy with the change. items.title: Samsung is holding back these 30+ Galaxy AI features for the Galaxy S27
items.summary:
Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 ties a long list of new Galaxy AI features to “Galaxy AI version 20271,” which Samsung’s own code labels as the S27’s AI version. 
 Gated Galaxy S27 features span Gallery’s Recompose, new Camera ProScan and Log LUT tools, full-table AI select, expanded Scam Detection languages, and an Audio eraser for your calls. 
 Several 20271 features, including Gen Video credits, Samsung Browser’s Ask anything, and Now Brief’s Bixby action card, appear tied to a paid Galaxy AI Premium tier. 
 Samsung brought several S26 features to older phones this year, so not all of these may stay Galaxy S27-exclusive forever. 

Over the past week, we’ve found dozens of new Galaxy AI features in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra , but many refuse to run on the device. When we dug into Samsung’s Scam Detection features for third-party calling apps , we noticed they check for something called “ Galaxy AI version 20271 ,” a level our S26 Ultra doesn’t meet. Now, we’ve found code that spells out what that number means: It’s the Galaxy S27’s AI version. We’ve gone through code across numerous apps in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 firmware on our Galaxy S26 Ultra, and here’s every Galaxy AI feature we’ve found so far that appears to be reserved for the Galaxy S27.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung’s code calls it the “S27” AI version 
 Every Galaxy phone with Galaxy AI carries an AI version number in its firmware, and Samsung’s apps check that number before…

items.title: Google app’s Images tab may get a major redesign with more control over your feed
items.summary:
TL;DR 

The Google app is working on a revamp of the Images tab that brings some of its elements front and center. 
 Additionally, we have discovered a new “Tune your feed” option to customize the images that appear on your feed. 
 Google could also let users ask questions inside a specific collection with a new Ask Anything button. 

It’s been over a year since the Google app rolled out the Pinterest-style Images tab , and it could soon get a makeover. For the uninitiated, the Images tab offers a feed of images based on your interests, letting you browse, search, or save items. Google is now testing a big redesign of this tab, along with a couple of new AI features for feed customization and collection-related queries.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

The existing Images tab includes a “For you” chip at the top, flanked by shortcuts to one of your existing collections and Saves. This Saves page includes tabs for All saved images and Collections. In version 17.78.14 of the Google app, we’ve activated a revamped Images tab, which brings all these elements together.
items.t: Google app’s Images tab may get a major redesign with more control over your feed

items.title: Google’s AI Mode could soon get a dedicated Library, pinned chats, and thread renaming
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is preparing to add a dedicated Library section to AI Mode, giving users a central hub to access, share, and download their AI-generated content. 
 AI Mode could also gain the ability to pin, unpin, and rename conversations, bringing its organizational tools closer to those of Gemini. 
 We also spotted redesigned icons for the Google app’s Home, Search, and Images tabs. None of these changes are publicly available yet. 

Google is preparing to give AI Mode some much-needed organizational tools, including a new library section to manage creations, the ability to pin and unpin conversations, the option to rename threads, and more. If these tools sound familiar, that’s because they are.

All the tools and functionality mentioned above are already an integral part of the Gemini experience, and it only makes sense for Google to port them over to AI Mode.

items.title: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases
items.summary:
TL;DR 

The removable back panels on the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite can accidentally detach when removing a protective case. 
 The issue occurs even with Amazon’s official cover, but hasn’t been observed on the aluminum Kindle or Paperwhite Signature Edition. 
 Amazon says owners can simply press the panel back into place, although reassembly can cause alignment issues. 

We got our first hint that Amazon was preparing to make Kindle batteries easier to replace back in May, and the company delivered on that front with the launch of its redesigned Kindle lineup in October. It’s a welcome change for devices that people often keep for years, but some owners of the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite are discovering that the removable back panel can come loose long before it’s time for a new battery.

A Kindle owner on Reddit demonstrated how their Ube Kindle comes apart when removing a protective case. TikTok creator Jackie’s Book Tally shared a similar experience, showing how trying to peel away a clear case to put some stickers on the back of her Kindle causes the device’s housing to separate.
items.t: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases

items.title: Gemini Live is testing a new Activity tab for all your agentic tasks

 These two tabs should let users check on their existing one-time tasks or ones they’ve scheduled to run periodically.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

items.title: Google Health won’t let users manually add rests between workout sets
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Health’s manual workout builder lacks the option to schedule rests between sets, even though the Premium-exclusive Health Coach supports it. 
 Live workout metrics can also fail to appear in the app, even with an active smartwatch connection. 
 We’ve reached out to Google to find out whether fixes are in the works and when users can expect them. 

One of the biggest fitness upgrades in the November Pixel Drop lets Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 owners follow workouts directly on their wrists, with timers and audio cues that tell them when to move on to the next set or exercise. But as more users get access to step-by-step workouts , a scheduling limitation for rest between sets and a bug affecting live workout metrics are taking some of the shine off the experience.

Multiple Google Health users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) report that while they can schedule rest periods between different exercises when building a custom workout, they can’t do the same between sets of an individual exercise.
items.t: Google Health won’t let users manually add rests between workout sets

items.title: Global Xiaomi 17 Ultra starts receiving HyperOS 4
items.summary:
Xiaomi announced the HyperOS 4 update schedule earlier this month, but it seems to have missed the deadline for some of its phones, including the flagship Xiaomi 17 Ultra. Our office unit received the update just this morning, bringing some of the new features that debuted with the Xiaomi 18 Pro series and new aesthetics.

Surprisingly, we got the update without any confirmation. The handset updated itself overnight, which is the first time we have experienced this sort of thing.

items.title: Last call for Amazon UK's top Black Friday deals: flagships, foldables, mid-rangers and more
items.summary:
The week of sales preceding Black Friday is coming to an end – but you still have enough time to pick up a new smartphone on sale. In fact, the prices of several models have gone down since the sales started. The prices of foldables in particular have seen notable downward corrections since last week – for example, a 12/512GB Galaxy Z Fold8 was £1,600 last week and is £1,400 now.

Some of the non-folding phones got cheaper too. Most models are still in stock, but a few are no longer available, e.g. the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max and the Sony Xperia 1 VIII.
